why: Judge 1 is right. V4 is 'v4 as it is' (SPACE 4.2) and takes no fix (AMENDMENTS 3); both judges pass it on v4's own runs (DEP-01, DEP-03, DEP-04), so its own failed run counts the same way. Confirmed step by step: (1) v4 reports no caught-up number (none in api/; STATUS.md lists 'a public caught-up signal' as the platform's first need), and it opens its write gate by membership, not by the rows it holds (api/index.ts, `membership.gate`); (2) STATUS.md records a member back inside the eviction window that says writable about 100 ms before it holds its peers' rows; (3) that run is this requirement's own acceptance test. The per-peer tails in kernel/confirm.ts could feed a fix, but the fix is not in the row.

Judge 1 is right. Confirmed step by step: (1) a v4 member whose fold is empty at boot applies its `data:` seed, and on first contact with a cluster 'fresh keys ride in' (api/index.ts, the seed's own comment); (2) a deleted row's tombstone is collected within a heartbeat (tombstone GC, kernel/log.ts), so nothing is left to say the key was deleted; (3) so a fresh joiner's seed row looks new and last-writer-wins spreads it: the deleted row came back in 2 runs of 2 on v4 63e0679, which is this requirement's own regression case (STATUS.md). The skip-seed-on-join fix is not in the row, and V4 takes no fix (AMENDMENTS 3).

The design gives this one line: a seed applies at create, and the catalog keeps a 'seed applied' mark (DESIGN-V5 4.2 and 6.1; in `#meta`, or in the row's own controller or manifest), so a joining copy folds the log and never seeds. But the mark and the seed rows sit in two places, and nothing ran a crash between the two or two creators at once. E-33's 'seeds' are founding members, not `data:` seeds, and API.md still asks who creates a resource (Q-A1).

why: Judge 1 is right, and it matches PERF-02 to PERF-07, where both judges fail V4 on the same fact. Confirmed step by step: (1) v4's shell runs one write and one fsync per persist call, in order, and its own comment says many appends per fsync is not built (shell/runtime.ts, `persist`); (2) so single-row writes share no fsync; (3) STATUS.md measured about 250 persisted writes a second per member, and 10,000 single-row writes not all on disk in 20 s, against PERF-09's 50,000: 99.5 % under the bar. Group commit would be a change to the row, and V4 takes no fix (AMENDMENTS 3).

Judge 2 is right. BUY is JetStream first (SPACE 4.1); it was built on JetStream (E-44) and priced on it (E-41), and both judges of PERF-02, PERF-05, PERF-06 and PERF-07 fail BUY on this same ceiling. On JetStream `persisted` is `sync_interval: always`, which fsyncs each message alone whatever the batching: 3,668 messages a second from one async publisher and 3,275 from 16 clients (E-09b), against PERF-09's 50,000, and fero cannot change the store. A Redpanda base would pass (175,420 a second, E-09d), but that is not the base the row was run on.

Judge 1 is right. E-02's followers are log nodes in shape: each appends the writer's batch to its journal, runs one fdatasync per batch and acks, and the batch commits when a quorum is durable: 2.8 million 100 B appends a second in TS. The log-first draft's node keeps a journal (V5-LOG-FIRST-REVIEW), and even a file per loglet, the form both judges pass ISR on, shares each fsync and reaches 0.59 to 2.25 million appends a second (E-12), against 50,000. The seal and the shared tier's budget belong to other requirements.

Judge 2 is right. BUY as run (E-44) and as shaped for costing (E-41) keeps its log on three NATS servers of the project's own, with the app's two machines beside them as clients: the shape of SRV and PD, which both judges score 'not'. Every JetStream replica is a full copy (three per stream in E-44), so there is no log-only voter and no platform tier that stands in as the third, and a project cannot run on two copies. A crash of an app machine is harmless, but that is as true of SRV; a NATS tier shared by projects would be SLOG's shape, and it was not run, priced or checked against OPS-14.

Judge 1 is right. Confirmed step by step: (1) v4's box directory is a registry from a name to listen addresses, and it hands each server every other server registered under its name (api/directory.ts); (2) v4 has no project: nothing in a dir, a registration or a HELLO names one; (3) so two unrelated apps with the same name and contract join: two `todos` servers showed each other's rows within seconds (STATUS.md, 2026-10-21), the requirement's own regression case. STATUS.md calls 'same name, same object' the design and a project scope 'a decision'; a secret keeps strangers out only where one is set.
